description: Still laying in stores for a hand that stopped coming. Crowd this brown handful of spines and the quills stay in.
lore: Small when it fell and small now: a brown handful with a soft tan face, four pale feet, and a black eye with a bit of light left in it. It travels along the bottom of things — walls, hedge-lines, the low side of a path — because that is where it went before, and it has kept the route long after the route stopped leading anywhere.

The nuts are the part that gives it away. It carries a fistful of hard glossy kernels, streaked tan and brown, and will not be parted from them, and a hedgehog has no use for a nut and never had. Somewhere behind this one there was a person who put food out at an hour, and an animal that learned to be at the place when they did, and of that whole arrangement the piece that lasted is the being-there. It is still laying in stores. It could not tell you who for. It could not have told you at the time either, which is somehow the worse half of it.

Rust is what it comes down to, which is not what anybody expects out of something soft. The stone comes out of it looking like old iron gone sour, weeping copper from every slit, and it has looked exactly that way since the hour it was picked out of the grass and it will look that way for good — a rust that has finished happening. The likeliest account of why is also the least dramatic. This animal spent its whole existence underneath the things people leave outdoors: a spade, a gate hinge, a length of chain lying in wet grass, all of it going quietly off in the weather while the hedgehog went past at the same hour every night for years together. It did not keep the person. It kept what the weather does to what the person left behind. Set against a blade it puts more into a blow than the blade earned, and armour that stops the blow starts giving up shortly afterwards, on its own schedule and not the wearer's.

One other thing turns up among its leavings and it is worth stopping over. A coarse black pelt, matted into clumps, three of its quills driven through and left in. Two animals on the low side of a path in the dark, both running on habit, neither of them choosing any part of what happened between them. Something out there is going about patchy now, and the hedgehog has been carrying the evidence on its back ever since, snagged in among the spines, because it has no way of putting anything down.
